statement_verbatim:
statement: A feature must not exceed 2 new tables, 2 async jobs, or 2 integrations; exceeding any hard
  limit MUST trigger a split.

statement: A feature slug (the 3rd segment of feature:<capability>:<name>) must be verb-object
  — kebab-case, at least two tokens, the leading token a verb from the convention verb
  lexicon, and no connective tokens. Brand or proper-noun slugs must be listed explicitly
  in feature.convention.yaml verb_object_enforcement.brand_exceptions; an implicit
  exception is a violation.
statement: Feature YAMLs declare a urn, a status, and a non-empty acceptance section.

statement: Final feature size = max(desired-outcome-count size, Footprint size); features MUST be S or smaller, else
  split or stage before execution.

statement: A feature URN is feature:{capability}:{feature}, both kebab-case, the feature in verb-object form;
  built via URNBuilder.feature.

statement: A feature's size must equal max(DESIRED OUTCOME size, Footprint size); features exceeding component/event/hard
  limits must be split.

statement: The artifact type (event, state, data, config) determines the appropriate
  verbs for the feature name.

statement: A flow router is the domain-decomposition artifact for a diverging journey
  — it declares WHICH user/system flow is selected next when a journey branches, keyed by a produced
  artifact (the divergence signal), composing multiple strictly-linear user/system flows into a
  branching journey-of-journeys. It is a declared routing registry (artifact_urn ->
  user_system_flow_id), not an imperative map. This names the routing DECISION; the runtime that
  resolves and executes it (the route-control runner and its dispatcher) is a coder/tester
  concern. This node is an advisory semantic anchor — it enforces nothing directly;
  the enforceable parts of this meaning are decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes
  that require it.

statement: Every entry in plan/_user_system_flows/_flow_routers.yaml must agree with the document
  it points at on every field it mirrors — theme, status and surfaces. The document
  is authoritative; the registry is discovery metadata, so a disagreement is always
  the registry being wrong.

statement: Every acceptance embedded in a DESIRED OUTCOME is an object whose `identity.urn` starts with `acc:`. Package rule,
  strict.

statement: Every participant and lifeline a flow router lists is either an external actor (`user:…`, `system:…`)
  or a typed reference to an artifact the plan declares. Package rule, strict.

statement: Every plan artifact whose kind the planner recognizes carries its canonical identity (`user_system_flow_id`, `flow_router_id`,
  `journey_id`, or `urn`). Package rule, strict.

statement: No two plan artifacts declare the same identity (`user_system_flow_id`, `flow_router_id`, `journey_id`, `urn`,
  …). Package rule, strict.
statement: Every `.yaml`, `.yml` or `.json` file under `plan/` parses. Package rule, strict.

statement: Every typed reference an artifact makes (`capability:`, `feature:`, `desiredOutcome:`, `user-system-flow:`, `flowRouter:`, `journey:`)
  names an artifact the plan declares. `contract:` references are resolved by the contract registry rules instead.
  Package rule, strict.

statement: Every recognized plan artifact (product capability, feature, DESIRED OUTCOME and its acceptances, user/system flow, user/system flow flow router,
  journey topology, registries) satisfies its JSON Schema in `planner-schemas/`. A violation that belongs to a canonical
  rule is reported under that rule (for example `planner.user-system-flow.naming`); every other violation is reported here.
  Package rule, strict.
statement: Every product capability a user/system flow lists under `capabilities:` is declared as `capability:<slug>`. Package rule, strict.

statement: Artifact names map to REST API endpoints of the form /{domain}s/{id}/{resource}[/{category}],
  with the resource term selecting the HTTP verb (POST/GET/PUT/DELETE) and category
  facets adding path segments.
